items.title: Woman killed after being ‘swept into the water’ at Mississauga park
items.summary: The identity of a woman who fell into Lake Ontario at a Mississauga park and later died in hospital has not yet been made public as police try to locate her family. m. on Saturday night. , police added. The woman was rushed to hospital, where she was pronounced dead a short time later. “At this time, we have not been able to locate and notify her next of kin,” police said on Monday morning, adding no further details will be released until such a notification has taken place. Police did not reveal the age of the woman or any other details related to circumstances that may have led to her ending up in the water. It’s also not known if the woman was alone or with any other people prior to the mishap and her fall into the lake. Covering more than 20 acres, Jack Darling Memorial Park is one of the largest and most popular of the city’s waterfront green spaces. Situated on Lake Ontario a few kilometres west of Port Credit Harbour, where the Credit River empties into the lake, it features numerous amenities that include picnic areas, tennis courts, beach areas, a leash-free zone, a spray pad and two playgrounds. A section of the popular Waterfront Trail also runs through the park.

items.title: 5 charged, including 2 youths, in fatal double shooting on Brampton school grounds
items.summary: A 21-year-old and two 17-year-olds from Brampton are facing two charges each of first-degree murder, after a shooting on school grounds in Brampton that took the lives of one man and one youth in April, Peel police say.

items.title: Major road partially closed as new storm sewer installed in Mississauga
items.summary: Motorists who use a major road in Mississauga’s east end will face some delays this week as part of the route has been shut down due to construction. A Peel Region project to replace a storm sewer on a section of Dixie Road between Blundell Road and Caterpillar Road, south of Dundas Street East and north of The Queensway East, will close all southbound lanes to traffic starting today and continuing through Friday, officials said. Mississauga Ward 1 Coun. Stephen Dasko said in an online notice to residents the closure on the main north-south road is in effect “night and day” this week from 80 metres south of Blundell Road to 180 metres north of Caterpillar Road. ” Map shows area of Dixie Road in Mississauga’s east end where traffic will be impacted all this week. The project is one of multiple similar initiatives already underway or planned in Mississauga as the city’s aging infrastructure is either replaced or upgraded. A short distance to the west of Dixie Road, residents in the Cooksville area of the city are being told they can expect partial park and trail closures in addition to construction noise and dust starting this summer as workers rehabilitate a “critical” piece of infrastructure. Peel Region crews will be working on upgrading the Lower Cooksville Trunk Sewer, a “critical underground system” that carries wastewater from area homes and businesses to treatment facilities, Mississauga Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla said in an earlier update to the community.

items.title: Large emergency response to house fire in Mississauga
items.summary: There was a large emergency response to a house fire in Mississauga overnight. m. on Monday. It happened on Gardenview Crescent, which is near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Thomas Street in the city’s west end. Police said occupants of the home were evacuated and neighbouring residences were also evacuated as a precaution. The fire appeared to be contained to one home, however. One person was taken to a hospital with minor smoke inhalation. Police said there was a “large deployment” of Mississauga firefighters and roads were closed in the area as crews responded. The motorcyclist — an adult male — was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said. Both vehicles involved in the collision remained at the scene. Lanes were reduced on Dundas Street as officers investigated. m. Monday, police said the accident scene had been cleared. There is no word on what may have caused the incident.

items.title: Be part of the magic: Apply to be a part of the 2026 Mississauga Santa Claus Parade
items.summary: Businesses, community groups, performers and volunteers are invited to help bring holiday magic to downtown Mississauga. m. in downtown Mississauga. Applications are now open for float entries and walking groups. The annual parade will kick off Mississauga’s holiday season, bringing together dazzling, illuminated floats, festive entertainment and family-friendly fun. The celebration will also feature the opening of the City’s largest outdoor ice rink and the lighting of the Christmas tree at Celebration Square. This year’s theme, Sauga’s Home for the Holidays, invites parade participants to showcase the traditions, cultures, stories, and people that make our city feel like home. Organizations interested in participating are encouraged to apply early. Businesses, community groups and performers can showcase their holiday spirit, creativity and community pride in Mississauga’s largest winter event. Applications that meet participant criteria will be reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and will close on September 30 or once the parade hits capacity. Interested in volunteering? We are looking for volunteers to be parade marshals, ambassadors, and staging support. Volunteer applications will close on November 3, 2026. For more information and to apply, visit the parade webpage.

items.title: Nine People Cling to Capsized Boat in Rough Lake Ontario Waters Off Port Credit
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Peel police rescued nine people Saturday evening after their boat capsized in rough conditions near Port Credit Harbour Marina in Mississauga. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, a Peel police spokesperson, told the Toronto Star that officers found the vessel flipped over roughly 50 metres south of the Ridgetown break wall, tossed by high winds and waves reaching two to three metres. Bell-Morena described the conditions as challenging, and said all nine people were found clinging to the overturned boat when officers arrived. The Toronto Star reports everyone involved suffered only minor abrasions, with no other injuries reported. Investigators said it remains unclear what type of boat was involved. Bell-Morena said the vessel was later located near rocks on the west side of the Credit River, but crews were unable to recover it because of hazardous weather conditions. The Canadian Coast Guard was notified of the incident, the Toronto Star reports.
